column2: Sin is remaining turned away, after knowledge, from the work of one's own hand; its contrary is to stand facing that same work as one's own and for what it is, in acknowledgment and, as far as it can rightly be done, in deed, which attention alone does not do. Repentance contains that contrary only once it arrives at that facing, and grace is that facing insofar as it is given.

Sin is remaining turned away, after knowledge, from the work of one's own hand. Its contrary is to stand facing that work as one's own and for what it is: in acknowledgment, and in whatever deed can rightly be done, which attention alone never reaches. Repentance contains that contrary only once it arrives there, and grace is that facing insofar as it is given.
